about:

The firm consults, designs, manufactures, installs, and manages a broad portfolio including acoustical treatment, telecommunications, security, solar, Wi-Fi, cable networking, voice over IP, computer networks, network security, home theater, digital signage, lighting, locks, shades, blinds, SCADA, energy monitoring, and automation. It holds a DOE vendor number (149246), a CAGE code (81P78) for military, federal, and state contracting, and a Hawaii contractor’s license (C-35167). No facility size or headcount figures are disclosed.

We Are More serves residential, commercial, and marine customers across the Big Island, Maui County, Oahu, and Kauai. Its client base includes federal agencies, the military, state government, and private homeowners and businesses seeking integrated smart technology solutions.

The company emphasizes its end-to-end service model—from consultation through installation and ongoing management—and its readiness for government contracting at all levels as key differentiators.

The shop provides end-to-end metal fabrication under one roof, including laser cutting, forming, machining, welding, finishing, powder coating, and quality control. The business remains family-owned and operated, now headquartered in Buckhannon, WV, and continues to serve the region as the state's largest independent broadline foodservice distributor.

The company stocks more than 9,000 items spanning fresh meats, seafood, frozen and refrigerated goods, and non-food supplies. Recent expansion added over 800 square feet of freezer capacity to support growing service territories across West Virginia, Virginia, and western Pennsylvania. Orders are handled through a personalized phone system where customers reach a live representative.

name: West Automotive Products
old_description: Founded in 1983. Our core service is the design, fabrication and delivery of clutch alignment tools that are used in aftermarket clutch kits for thousands of engine types. Using an injection mold process, we currently produce more than 200 unique clutch alignment tools for consumer automobiles, large rigs and agricultural vehicles across North America, in addition to Central American and overseas markets.
about:
West Automotive Products operates from Canby, Oregon, where it was founded in 1983 by mechanic and inventor Don West. West began by crafting wooden dowels to solve the difficulty of aligning clutch discs and flywheels during manual transmission repairs, later evolving the process to custom plastic injection molds that became the foundation of the company.

The company designs, fabricates, and delivers more than 200 unique clutch alignment tools for aftermarket clutch kits covering thousands of engine types. Production runs on an in-house injection molding process that uses 100 percent post-industrial plastic and re-fabricates all byproducts, eliminating industrial waste. Beyond alignment tools, the Oregon facility manufactures drink holders, quick-disconnect tools, transmission plugs, seal installers, and timing chain tools without outsourcing.

Customers include manufacturers of aftermarket clutch kits for consumer automobiles, heavy-duty trucks, and agricultural equipment across North America, Central America, and overseas markets. West Automotive works directly with clients' R&D departments to develop custom tools for new and existing applications, guaranteeing 100 percent fill rates on every purchase order and on-time delivery to meet production schedules.

West’s differentiator is a fully integrated, no-outsource operation backed by a 100 percent product-quality guarantee that offers replacement or full refund. The founder’s original insight — precision alignment for manual transmissions — still drives a product line that emphasizes waste-free molding and rapid response to evolving engine platforms.

old_description: West Memphis Steel is a full-line hot rolled service center located in West Memphis, AR. WMS is a leader in the region for carbon steel as well as first and second stage processed parts. WMS services Alabama, Arkansas, Kentucky, Mississippi, Missouri and Tennessee with next day deliveries while also maintaining weekly shipments nationwide. The combination of holding a huge inventory with processing capabilities has made WMS one of the most respected and reliable service centers in the Southeast.
about:
West Memphis Steel Corporation operates from West Memphis, Arkansas, where it was founded in 1978. The company has been owned since 1988 by President and CEO Byron P. Besser, who entered the business as the nephew of co‑owner Louis Barg and worked in sales before acquiring the operation.

The firm runs a full‑line hot‑rolled steel service center with three campuses in the West Memphis area. Its processing capabilities include precision sawing, shearing, brake pressing, flat‑bed laser and plasma cutting, tube laser cutting, robotic welding, drilling/tapping, and assembly and kitting. The company stocks a wide range of carbon‑steel products — hot‑rolled and pickled‑and‑oiled sheet, plate, structural shapes, tubing, pipe, bar grating, and expanded metal — and emphasizes just‑in‑time processing with next‑day delivery across Alabama, Arkansas, Kentucky, Mississippi, Missouri, and Tennessee, plus weekly shipments nationwide.

West Memphis Steel serves manufacturers, fabricators, and construction firms throughout the Southeast that require carbon‑steel plate, sheet, and structural components processed to first‑ and second‑stage specifications. Its customer base includes companies needing cut‑to‑length blanks, welded assemblies, and kitted kits for downstream production.

The company states its mission is to improve people’s lives and maintain a family‑style workplace where entrepreneurial spirit thrives, while delivering a customer‑service experience that exceeds expectations and enables customers to excel. It highlights its long‑tenured workforce — some with 30‑year careers — as a key differentiator.

The shop also delivers prototyping, reverse engineering, and maintenance and repair services for engines, prime movers, and turbochargers.

name: Western Energy Systems
old_description: Western Energy Systems is a distributor and systems integrator of combined heat and power (CHP) and distributed generation solutions, including switchgear. Offers fuel gas compressors, battery storage and other power systems, serving utility, commercial and industrial clients.
about:
Western Energy Systems, operating as Northeast-Western Energy Systems USA, LLC (NES-WES), is headquartered in Brea, California. The company traces its roots to 1964 and was acquired by the INNIO Group in 2023, bringing additional resources to its power generation and microgrid businesses. With over 50 years of experience in reciprocating engine power applications, NES-WES has evolved into a full-service integrator of combined heat and power (CHP) and distributed generation (DG) solutions.

NES-WES designs, engineers, and maintains CHP and DG systems ranging from 50 kW to 22 MW, with a focus on gaseous fuels including natural gas, biogas, propane, and syngas. The firm provides end-to-end integration of balance-of-plant components such as heat recovery, fuel gas handling, emissions control, cooling systems, switchgear, transformers, and power plant controls. Its engineering team performs electrical system studies, protective relaying, and relay coordination, while field project managers oversee installation, pre-commissioning, startup, and acceptance testing. The company employs between 200 and 499 people.

The company serves utility, industrial, commercial, institutional, and governmental customers. Notable projects include the Bergen County Wastewater Treatment plant, Covidien's New Haven CHP installation, Mount Joy Wire, landfill-gas-to-energy facilities, High Sierra California Cogeneration, and Techni-Cast industrial cogeneration. Clients typically seek to reduce energy costs, improve resilience, and lower carbon footprints.

NES-WES emphasizes a balance of innovative solutions and time-tested approaches, aiming to exceed customer expectations. The 2023 acquisition by INNIO Jenbacher strengthened its position in the power generation and microgrid markets, allowing it to offer fully integrated, climate-neutral energy solutions from a single source.

The company emphasizes its union‑trained workforce, adherence to SMACNA standards, locally sourced materials, and competitive pricing as key differentiators built over more than five decades in the HVAC industry.

name: Western Washington Sheet Metal
old_description: Angela joined the Western Washington Sheet Metal JATC in 2017 after transferring from the SM JATC in Las Vegas, where she had been employed since 2008. Her introduction to the sheet metal industry came through a friend who worked at the JATC and recommended it as a promising career path.
about:
Western Washington Sheet Metal JATC operates as a non-profit union training center headquartered in Everett, Washington, with a second campus in DuPont. The joint apprenticeship committee traces its roots to a sheet metal apprenticeship tradition spanning over 100 years, with the modern program structure in place since 1973. It is governed by a committee of six labor trustees from SMART Local 66 and six management trustees from SMACNA Western Washington.

The JATC runs a five-year sheet metal apprenticeship combining on-the-job training with classroom instruction across four disciplines: general sheet metal fabrication and installation, testing adjusting and balancing (TAB), HVAC service, and residential sheet metal. At any given time roughly 500 apprentices are enrolled, and the program graduates approximately 98 journey-level workers each year. Instruction is delivered by seven full-time instructors supported by three administrators and two support staff, collectively holding nearly 210 years of industry experience. Facilities include welding labs certified for SMAW and FCAW processes, and curriculum covers commissioning, controls, energy auditing, smoke control, and Bluebeam.

Graduates enter the workforce through 72 signatory contractors — ranging from small shops to large mechanical firms such as MacDonald-Miller, Hermanson Company, McKinstry, and PSF Mechanical — who employ apprentices and journey workers across commercial construction, healthcare facilities, data centers, and institutional projects. The DuPont campus hosts the SMART Heroes program, providing a direct entry route for active-duty military personnel and veterans. The program also partners with Bates Technical College for associate-degree credit.

The committee’s stated mission is to bring labor and management together to develop a highly skilled, competitive workforce for the evolving sheet metal industry. By offering tuition-free training, zero student debt, and a clear path to union wages and benefits — including retirement, family medical, dental, and vision — the JATC positions the apprenticeship as a career alternative to traditional college pathways.
